statement: J.N.B. Hewitt (Tuscarora ethnologist/linguist, Bureau of American Ethnology), Iroquoian Cosmology, published in two parts by the Smithsonian (Part 1, 1903; Part 2, 1928), is the authoritative comparative scholarly source for the Haudenosaunee creation narrative — deliberately preserving three separate versions (Onondaga, Seneca, Mohawk) as literal translations rather than flattening them into one composite myth. Sky Woman's actual name varies genuinely by nation and language (Ataensic/Ataentsic, Huron form; Iagentci/Awenhai, Seneca; Iotsitsisonh/Atsiʼtsiaka:ion, Mohawk) — "Sky Woman" is a descriptive English title, not a proper name in any one language, and should not be treated as if it were.

sources.citation: Hewitt, J.N.B. "Iroquoian Cosmology." Bureau of American Ethnology, Twenty-First Annual Report (Part 1, 1903) and Forty-Third Annual Report (Part 2, 1928). Washington, DC: Smithsonian Institution.
sources.author: J.N.B. Hewitt

does_not_demonstrate: That "Sky Woman" is a single pan-Haudenosaunee proper name rather than an English descriptive title standing in for genuinely distinct per-nation names
